title: The Good Samaritan
text:
An expert in the law asked Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life. Love God, and love your neighbor as yourself, came the answer. The lawyer, wanting to justify himself, asked, "And who is my neighbor?" Jesus replied with a story.

A man was going down the steep road from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell among robbers. They stripped him, beat him and left him half dead by the road. A priest happened to come that way, saw him, and passed by on the other side. A Levite, an assistant at the Temple, did the same.

Then a Samaritan came along, a member of a people the Jews of that time despised. When he saw the man, he was moved with pity. He went to him, poured oil and wine on his wounds and bandaged them. He put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day he gave the innkeeper two silver coins and said, "Look after him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back."

"Which of these three," Jesus asked, "was a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?" The lawyer said, "The one who showed him mercy." Jesus told him, "Go and do likewise."
lesson: Do not ask who deserves your help; ask who needs it in front of you. Kindness that crosses group lines is the kind that counts.
people: A traveler, a priest, a Levite, a Samaritan
location: Road from Jerusalem to Jericho, Judea (modern Israel and West Bank)
